newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka oil refinery to resume work by Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka oil refinery to resume work by Thursday.

text.p: Sri Lanka's only oil refinery, run by the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC), may resume opertions by June 12 after an unscheduled shutdown, officials said on Monday.
"Earlier we expected to recommence on Monday or Tuesday. Now we have pushed it back to June 12," said a CPC official who declined to be identified.

The 50,000-60,000 barrel-per-day capacity refinery was shut down on May 30 because of insufficient crude supply after the CPC's single point mooring buoy (SPMB), which discharges crude from tankers to the refinery, was damaged in an accident.
"The problem with the SPMB is settled and it is operating normally," the official said.

But he said the refinery has not yet achieved necessary operating levels as one of the tankers, carrying 60,000 tonnes of crude, was currently discharging crude throuh the SPMB at a slower rate due to a problem with the tanker.
"The necessary levels for us to operate can't be achieved immediately due to a slower discharge rate of one tanker," he said.
Another tanker carrying 85,000 tonnes of crude was waiting outside Colombo port.
CPC has a crude oil storage capacity of 150,000 tonnes.
